_comment: The maintainer's OWN prompt library, recovered from the PixelLab account. They completed the entire X-over-Y matrix once before this project started; the art is unusable (a mis-click changed the camera angle) but the WORDING is the most valuable thing we have — it is the vocabulary that actually produced clean tiles, found by hand over hundreds of attempts. Retry counts are real data: the hard pairs took 7-9 sheets before one came out clean, so budget for that rather than expecting a first-shot hit.

_connectors._note: all three were used interchangeably; none is obviously better from counts alone

_qualifiers._note: NOTE these sit alongside MATERIAL nouns (snow, black rock, lava, grass, ice, dirt, water, stone, sand beach, soil) rather than replacing them. That matters: our own bake-off found a bare #hex gives the flattest, most colour-accurate TOP — but flatness is exactly what the WALLS must not have, since they build every cliff face. Naming the material is what keeps wall texture alive.
